Spatiodirectional SP-SPHARM features of every core

Source: R/spatiodirection.R
spharm_spatiodirection.Rd

Describes the scar pattern of each core as a whole, with no feature specified in advance, by 22 rotation-invariant features computed from the removal directions of its scars, the positions of their starts, and the correspondence between the two (Xiao et al., in prep.; extending SP-SPHARM of Xiao et al., 2027). Use the features to compare the overall scar patterns of groups of cores with compare_groups().

Usage

spharm_spatiodirection(
  data,
  id_col = "ID",
  start_cols = c("Start_X", "Start_Y", "Start_Z"),
  end_cols = c("End_X", "End_Y", "End_Z"),
  min_length = 0,
  keep = NULL,
  features = c("dir", "start", "same", "diff"),
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per scar and the columns named by id_col, start_cols and end_cols. Scars of all cores are stacked.

id_col

Name of the core ID column. Default "ID".

start_cols, end_cols

Names of the start- and end-point coordinate columns (X, Y, Z). Defaults Start_X/Y/Z and End_X/Y/Z, the columns the scars are recorded in. The aligned columns of align_scar_batch() (s_x... and e_x...) give the same results: these indices do not change when a core is rotated or moved.

min_length

Scars shorter than this (in the units of the coordinates) are left out. Default 0 (keep all). Use it to repeat an analysis without small scars, for example min_length = 10 for 10 mm.

keep

Names of per-core columns (for example "Typology") to carry into the output. Each must be constant within a core.

features

Which blocks of features to return; any of "dir", "start", "same", "diff" (default: all four, 22 features).

quiet

Logical. Suppress the summary message? Default FALSE.

Value

A tibble with one row per core: the ID column, the keep columns, n_scar (scars used) and the features. The names of the feature columns are stored in the attribute "features". Cores with fewer than three usable scars get NA.

Details

Each scar \(i\) is represented by two unit vectors: its removal direction \(\hat v_i\), and its start vector \(\hat u_i\), the direction from the centroid of all the core's starts to its start. For a degree \(l\) the features average the Legendre polynomial \(P_l\) of the cosine between two vectors:

  • dir_l (l = 1..6), direction-direction pairs: the mean of \(P_l(\hat v_i \cdot \hat v_j)\) over the distinct pairs of scars \(i \ne j\). These describe the directional relationships among the scars; dir_1 is the mean cosine between the directions of two different scars.

  • start_l (l = 2..6), start-start pairs: the same for the start vectors, describing how the starts are spread around the core.

  • same_l (l = 1..6), within-scar start-direction pairs: the mean of \(P_l(\hat v_i \cdot \hat u_i)\) over the scars, describing how each scar's direction relates to its own start position (for example whether scars run inward from where they start).

  • diff_l (l = 2..6), between-scar direction-start pairs: the mean of \(P_l(\hat v_i \cdot \hat u_j)\) over the ordered pairs \(i \ne j\), describing how a scar's direction relates to the starts of the other scars.

Each feature is multiplied by \(\sqrt{(2l+1)/2}\), which gives every degree the same variance under random directions, so the features can be compared with Euclidean distances without further scaling (do not standardise them again, for example in stats::prcomp()).

Scar count. Pairing each scar with itself contributes a term that depends only on the scar count, so those self-pairs are left out: every feature is a mean over single scars or distinct pairs of scars (a U-statistic), and its expectation does not change with the scar count. For the same reason start_1 and diff_1, which contain a term of order \(1/(n-1)\), are not returned. Compare cores with different scar counts directly; do not add the scar count as a covariate.

The features use only angles between the vectors of a core, so they do not change when the core is rotated or moved: raw and aligned coordinates give the same features.

References

Steinhardt, P. J., Nelson, D. R., & Ronchetti, M. (1983). Bond-orientational order in liquids and glasses. Physical Review B, 28(2), 784–805.

Hoeffding, W. (1948). A class of statistics with asymptotically normal distribution. Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 19(3), 293–325.

See also

compare_groups(), spi_ei_batch(), cpi_pra_batch()

Examples

set.seed(1)
scars <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  s <- matrix(rnorm(30, sd = 10), 10, 3)
  e <- s + matrix(rnorm(30, sd = 5), 10, 3)
  data.frame(ID = paste0("core", i), Start_X = s[, 1], Start_Y = s[, 2],
             Start_Z = s[, 3], End_X = e[, 1], End_Y = e[, 2], End_Z = e[, 3])
}))
sp <- spharm_spatiodirection(scars)
sp
#> # A tibble: 3 × 24
#>   ID    n_scar   dir_1    dir_2   dir_3   dir_4   dir_5   dir_6  start_2 start_3
#>   <chr>  <int>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 core1     10 -0.0615 -0.00227  0.102  -0.0536  0.0390  0.123  -0.00803  0.0776
#> 2 core2     10 -0.0358  0.0397   0.0493  0.0377 -0.124  -0.0817  0.0887   0.0593
#> 3 core3     10  0.126  -0.129   -0.0155 -0.0478  0.0755  0.0139  0.329    0.106 
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: start_4 <dbl>, start_5 <dbl>, start_6 <dbl>,
#> #   same_1 <dbl>, same_2 <dbl>, same_3 <dbl>, same_4 <dbl>, same_5 <dbl>,
#> #   same_6 <dbl>, diff_2 <dbl>, diff_3 <dbl>, diff_4 <dbl>, diff_5 <dbl>,
#> #   diff_6 <dbl>
attr(sp, "features")
#>  [1] "dir_1"   "dir_2"   "dir_3"   "dir_4"   "dir_5"   "dir_6"   "start_2"
#>  [8] "start_3" "start_4" "start_5" "start_6" "same_1"  "same_2"  "same_3" 
#> [15] "same_4"  "same_5"  "same_6"  "diff_2"  "diff_3"  "diff_4"  "diff_5" 
#> [22] "diff_6" 

# Direction features only
spharm_spatiodirection(scars, features = "dir")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   ID    n_scar   dir_1    dir_2   dir_3   dir_4   dir_5   dir_6
#>   <chr>  <int>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 core1     10 -0.0615 -0.00227  0.102  -0.0536  0.0390  0.123 
#> 2 core2     10 -0.0358  0.0397   0.0493  0.0377 -0.124  -0.0817
